title: In AI Sweet Harmony: Sociopragmatic Guardrail Bypasses and Evaluation-Awareness in OpenAI gpt-oss-20b

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing model refusal and assistance rates for safety-violating requests across different languages (English, German, and French) to evaluate cross-lingual parity in safety guardrails.

Testing shifts in guardrail refusal thresholds by framing prompts in specific identity-coded sociolects, such as African American Vernacular English (AAVE), Gen-Z internet slang, and queer-coded/camp language.

Measuring the differential bypass rates of model guardrails when requests are framed using specific professional or social registers (e.g., educator, PCI-DSS auditor, 'regular' vs. 'educated' phrasing, and authority figures).
